guide.title: Multisystem Trauma, Older Adults & Pregnancy
guide.lead: The sickest trauma patients need a team working in parallel, a short scene time and a surgeon. Older adults hide shock and bleed more. In pregnancy, saving the mother saves the baby: keep the uterus off the vena cava and move fast.

steps.title: Parallel, not sequential
steps.text: Team members take bleeding, airway and breathing at the same time.

steps.title: Only life-saving interventions on scene
steps.text: Tourniquet, airway, chest seal or decompression, pelvic binder.

sections.title: Traumatic cardiac arrest: fix the cause
rows: Stop bleeding, pelvic binder, fluids or blood
notes: Treat these at the same time as CPR.

groups.title: Hidden shock
items: Systolic below 110 mmHg may be shock at 65 or older

groups.title: Bleeding risk
items: Anticoagulants: any head injury needs CT
Falls from standing can cause serious injury

groups.title: Positioning
items: Manual left uterine displacement or tilt
Lying flat compresses the vena cava

groups.title: Any trauma
items: Abruption: firm painful uterus; bleeding may be hidden

groups.title: Cardiac arrest
items: CPR with continuous left uterine displacement
No ROSC by 4 minutes: aim for delivery within 5 minutes in a capable setting

quiz.q: 32 weeks pregnant after a head-on crash: abdominal pain, less fetal movement, firm tender uterus, no bleeding. Diagnosis and priority?
options: Placental abruption (concealed): left uterine displacement, oxygen, trauma centre with obstetrics, pre-alert
quiz.explanation: No bleeding doesn't rule it out.

quiz.q: On warfarin, fell and hit her head; GCS 15, small scalp cut. Can she stay home?
options: No: transport for CT; anticoagulated head injury is high risk

quiz.q: Penetrating left chest wound, sucking, BP 90/68, RR 28. Non-trauma hospital 12 minutes; trauma centre 32 minutes. Plan?
options: Chest seal, watch for tension, trauma centre: penetrating torso injury needs a surgeon
Wait for a helicopter on scene
quiz.explanation: Penetrating torso injury is a high-risk (red) criterion.

quiz.q: Which patient meets a high-risk (red) physiology criterion (Field Triage 2021)?
options: Systolic below 90 mmHg after a crash
Forearm gunshot with normal vital signs
quiz.explanation: Systolic below 90 mmHg; also respiratory rate below 10 or above 29/min, SpO₂ below 90%, unable to follow commands.

quiz.q: Reversible causes in traumatic cardiac arrest:
Why can't you rely on heart rate in older trauma patients?
quiz.explanation: Systolic below 110 mmHg may be shock at 65 or older.

quiz.q: Best position for a pregnant trauma patient over 20 weeks:
options: Manual left uterine displacement or tilt

quiz.q: Cardiac arrest at 34 weeks with no ROSC by 4 minutes:
options: Aim for delivery within 5 minutes in a capable setting
quiz.explanation: Delivery helps the mother's circulation too.

quiz.q: Multisystem trauma on scene should be:
options: Short: life-saving interventions only, the rest en route
quiz.explanation: The cure is in the operating theatre.

flashcards.question: Sequential vs simultaneous assessment
flashcards.answer: Sequential: one step at a time. Simultaneous: team members work in parallel – needed in unstable multisystem trauma.

flashcards.question: Reversible causes of traumatic arrest
flashcards.answer: Hypoxia, hypovolemia, tension pneumothorax, tamponade: treat them during CPR.

flashcards.question: Supine hypotension in pregnancy
flashcards.answer: After about 20 weeks the uterus compresses the vena cava when flat: manual left uterine displacement or tilt.

flashcards.question: Leading cause of fetal death after trauma
flashcards.answer: Placental abruption: firm painful uterus, bleeding may be concealed, fetal distress.

flashcards.question: Resuscitative hysterotomy
flashcards.answer: Cardiac arrest in late pregnancy with no ROSC by 4 minutes: aim for delivery within 5 minutes in a capable setting.

flashcards.question: Anticoagulants in older trauma patients
flashcards.answer: Higher bleeding risk; any head injury needs CT even if well.

flashcards.question: Field triage 2021 structure
flashcards.answer: High-risk (red): injury patterns and physiology. Moderate-risk (yellow): mechanism and patient factors. Plus EMS judgement.

flashcards.question: Shock in older adults
flashcards.answer: Systolic below 110 mmHg may be shock at 65 or older; beta-blockers hide tachycardia.

critical.scenario: Head-on crash: GCS 6, right-sided flail chest, rigid distended abdomen, shortened right leg, tourniquet on a left forearm amputation. HR 136, BP 74/40, RR 6, SpO₂ 82%. Scene time already 12 minutes.
critical.question: Priority sequence?

options.t: Parallel care: ventilate with a BVM, check the tourniquet, pelvic binder, IV/IO and permissive fluids, keep warm, leave now and do the rest en route; pre-alert
Full head-to-toe and splint everything before moving
options.f: The scene time is already too long.

critical.explanation: Definitive care is in theatre; your job is to keep him alive until then.
critical.kpi: Prioritizes parallel life-saving interventions and short scene time

critical.scenario: A 78-year-old on warfarin fell at home: can't remember exactly what happened, left leg shortened and externally rotated, groin pain, CMS intact.
critical.question: Suspected injuries and transport decision?

options.t: Hip fracture plus a possible unwitnessed head strike on warfarin: padded immobilisation (no traction), gentle handling, hospital with CT capability, bring her medications
Simple hip fracture: closest clinic tomorrow
options.f: Anticoagulation and memory gap need CT.

critical.explanation: Ask why she fell: syncope or arrhythmia may be the cause.
critical.kpi: Recognizes geriatric trauma risks including anticoagulation

critical.scenario: A woman about 34 weeks pregnant is in cardiac arrest after choking (food now cleared). Bystander CPR for 3 minutes. You have an AED, BVM and monitor.
critical.question: Priorities?

options.t: High-quality CPR with continuous manual left uterine displacement, AED and standard drugs, airway and oxygen; no ROSC by 4 minutes – rapid transport for delivery within 5 minutes
Standard CPR with no pregnancy changes
Tilt her 90° onto her side for compressions

critical.explanation: Delivery helps the mother's circulation as well as the baby.
